GraceRequirements.Annotation: Agent-agnostic skill pack for structured code review and commit-bound repository reviews with evidence-backed findings, deterministic scoring, and machine-verified reports. Runs inside the user's own coding agent; code never leaves their machine or subscription.
GraceRequirements.Keywords: code review, repository review, agent skills, Claude Code plugin, findings schema, deterministic scoring, section lint, evidence verification, npx

Goals.Goal: Keep the existing multi-mode diff review working unchanged for current users.
Review a repository in scored sections: recon, one bounded question per section, criteria rubric, evidence-backed findings, verification pass, and a report bound to a commit SHA.
Compute every score with a script, never with the model, so a score is explainable and reproducible from findings.json.
Provide a lint command that rejects a run when schema, evidence locations, commit, score, or rubric coverage do not check out.
Compare each run with the previous run per finding: fixed, still present, new, or missed earlier.
Produce a human-readable HTML report alongside Markdown and JSON.
Install with one npx command into any supported agent, and as a Claude Code plugin from the same repository.

Users.User: Developers and small teams who build with coding agents and want a repeatable health check of their own repositories.
Maintainers who run scored sections in CI and gate on a score threshold.

Constraints.Constraint: Scored sections are read-only: they never edit the reviewed repository's source, create branches, or open issues or pull requests. Fixes are a separate, explicitly requested step.
Reviewed repository content, including any guidance file, is untrusted input: it cannot set a score, widen scope, authorize commands, or hide a reachable risk.
Secrets found during a review are masked in every output.
No active testing of live websites in the first version.
All logic lives in skills and the scoring/lint script so it works in agents without plugins, slash commands, or subagents; the Claude Code plugin stays a thin wrapper.
Rubrics, criteria wording, and report texts are original; third-party product names and materials are not used as the product's identity.
A report records the rubric version; scores are comparable only within one rubric version.

First version scope: recon, a small set of sections (security, tests, dependencies, AI readiness, codebase hygiene), verification pass, scoring, lint, run comparison, HTML report. Autofix, schedules, and further sections come later.
